activity_context.topic_title: Integrating Rational Functions with Irreducible Quadratic Factors

feedback.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+7$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+7}+\frac{C}{x+1}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+7)(x+1),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x+17 & =(Ax+B)(x+1)+C({x}^{2}+7).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-1,B=3,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)}=\frac{-x+3}{{x}^{2}+7}+\frac{2}{x+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{-x+3}{{x}^{2}+7}+\frac{2}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use a substitution $u={x}^{2}+7.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+7| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+7).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{7}}).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+2x+17}{({x}^{2}+7)(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+7}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+7)+3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{7}})+2\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+K \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+7)+\frac{3}{\sqrt{7}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{7}})+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+K\end{aligned}
$$
